claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do. I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 19 and still lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I understand you're inquiring about your son Alex, who is 19 and lives at home with you.

Since Alex is 19, his eligibility for Child Benefit depends on whether he's in approved education or training. 

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, full-time non-advanced education, or approved training such as certain courses at school or college)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. He's studying for his A-levels at the local sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. Studying for A-levels at sixth form college would typically count as approved education.

Now I need to understand your situation a bit more:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand your responsibility for Alex:

**Are you responsible for Alex? This typically means either:**
- **You live with him (which you've mentioned you do), or**
- **You're paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards his upkeep (things like food, clothes, or pocket money)**

Since Alex lives with you, this should normally mean you're responsible for him. Can you confirm that you provide for his day-to-day needs?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right. He lives with me and I provide for all his day-to-day needs - food, clothes, all of that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** (For example, Alex's other parent or another family member)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. A couple more questions:

**Has Alex started any paid work for 24 hours or more per week, or is he receiving any benefits in his own right** (such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't. He's just focused on his studies at the moment - no work and no benefits of his own.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for that information. Just one final question to complete my assessment:

**Do you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000?** 

(This doesn't affect your *eligibility* for Child Benefit, but it may mean you have to pay a High Income Child Benefit tax charge, so it's important to be aware of.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, I see. No, neither of us earns anywhere near that amount.

## Good News! You Are Eligible for Child Benefit

Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

### Here's why:

✓ **Alex is 19 and in approved education** - He's studying for his A-levels at sixth form college, which counts as approved education. You can claim Child Benefit for children under 20 who stay in approved education or training.

✓ **You live in the UK** - You meet the residency requirement.

✓ **You're responsible for Alex** - He lives with you and you provide for all his day-to-day needs.

✓ **No one else is claiming** - Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

✓ **Alex isn't working 24+ hours or claiming benefits** - He's focused on his studies and not receiving benefits in his own right.

### Additional Information:

Since neither you nor your partner earns over £60,000, you won't need to worry about the High Income Child Benefit tax charge.

### What to do next:

If you're not already receiving Child Benefit for Alex, you can make a claim. If you have any questions about how to claim, feel free to ask!
